meta.title: Bitcoin and AI with Jordi Visser
meta.speakers: Alex Thorn (host), Bimnet (Galaxy Trading), Jordi Visser (Visser Labs)
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · Bitcoin near a cycle bottom · hot CPI and an equity-supply problem · Jordi's odds-board method · agents and 'short friction' · AI is concentration, not a bubble · Bitcoin's belief moat and wealth becoming money

snapshot: Market desk (Bimnet, Galaxy Trading): Bitcoin ~**$81.5K**, 12 months past the prior high and 'within spitting distance' of a four-year-cycle bottom; the line in the sand is the falling 50-week average near $77K.
Macro is stressed: September CPI hot in almost every category (~3.8-3.9% annualized core), refined-fuel prices climbing, credit spreads widening; Nasdaq -2.14% on recording day.
Paul Tudor Jones (cited): Big Tech has gone from buybacks to issuing equity for data centers — 2027 equity flows the worst since 2004.
Jordi Visser's bull case for Bitcoin is **AI agents**: crypto rails were built for humans who don't care; agents will chase every spread ('crypto is margin compression').

AI is not a bubble to Jordi — no valuation bubble (Nvidia ~15x earnings vs Cisco's 100x), no fraudulent credit, demand exceeds supply — but higher rates create a **concentration** of few winners and many zombie losers.
Bitcoin's moat is belief, like gold and religion; he sees Mag 7 multiples compressing while Bitcoin outperforms them next — then 'greed kicks in'.
Endgame: tokenization turns illiquid wealth into spendable money, reducing new money creation; with humanoids doing the work, corporations get taxed.

themes.title: Bitcoin is near its four-year-cycle bottom — buy-the-range, not the tick
themes.lead: Bimnet sees a new cycle to fresh all-time highs ahead, whether the fill is $82K or $75K.
bullets: Weak since failing near $86.7K; dipped to almost $80K, rallied to $83.5K, now ~$81.5K. Bimnet: 'squarely in the stack sats time period'.
Four-year-cycle thesis: 12 months after the prior all-time high, the low is close — the gap between $82K, $75K or $70K is 'a little meaningless' long term.
Tactically: open interest is **low** and alts have had a healthy flush; lower prices remain possible and $80K may be tested again.
Bull/bear line: the 50-week moving average at **$77,195**, still falling as last October-November's high weeks roll off.
Long-dormant (5+ year) holders have been distributing; Bimnet thinks a low-basis OG whale wanted to sell in 2026 and, if not yet, should wait for 2027-28.
Rails headlines: a BNY-Citadel transaction, **Citi** partnering with Coinbase on stablecoins across 70 countries, a NYSE tokenized-stock settlement — 'the crypto rails are here to stay'.
Alex Thorn: Bitcoin holds up better than alts because 'it just had its bear market'; the S&P is still well ahead of it this year.

quote.text: I feel more confident than ever that, you know, we're entering a new cycle where you will hit um, you know, fresh all-time highs uh, in the coming years.

themes.watch: Galaxy is a crypto trading firm and facilitated the 80,000 BTC OG sale it tracks; the four-year cycle is Bimnet's own framework, not a consensus.

themes.title: Hot CPI, a refining squeeze and Big Tech issuing equity: caution warranted
themes.lead: Bimnet sees inflation, rising debt costs and worsening equity supply converging with the S&P only ~3% off its highs — time to think about hedging.
bullets: CPI hot in almost every category — cookies the rare decline. Core ~0.36 unrounded, **3.8-3.9%** annualized, above nearly all Bloomberg estimates despite dovish 'no October hike' Fed talk.

Diesel, heating oil and gasoline climbing; no global refining capacity, so even an Iran resolution leaves inventories to rebuild. The Russia diesel waiver is ~14 hours of supply; truckers had threatened to strike.
Rising nominal yields plus **widening credit spreads** with heavy sovereign, corporate and municipal issuance ahead.
Paul Tudor Jones (cited): tech went from buybacks to funding data centers with free cash flow to issuing equity — the 2027 flows picture is the worst since 2004.
Recording day: Nasdaq -2.14%, S&P -1.5%, VIX and the dollar up, long bonds bid — a flight to quality. The KOSPI took a hit on memory headlines and Chinese competition.
Positive catalysts still ahead: Q3 tech earnings, the **midterm election**, a possible Iran resolution. Broadcom's CEO said capital may be the bottleneck, not energy demand.
Endgame per Bimnet: government bailouts and QE, '6 months or 18 months' out.

quote.text: I don't think this Fed wants to be hiking uh but they're not going to be credible if they don't.

themes.title: Markets as a horse-racing odds board: bet the gap between your odds and the screen's
themes.lead: Liquidity is finite; when everyone piles into one horse it pays less — Jordi's edge is spotting where the room prices near-zero odds.
bullets: Son of a core driller who taught him horse handicapping, billiards, backgammon and chess; a book on compounding (10% a year for 50 years) pulled him into markets.
**Morgan Stanley** from 1992 at a $30,000 salary; opened the São Paulo office in his late 20s; left in 2003 after managing hundreds, tired of bonus entitlement — his best man died on 9/11.

At George Weiss' firm from 2005: 2007-2009 produced **90%** of his lifetime earnings. The multistrat raised $3 billion, then lost two-thirds of assets as Swiss fund-of-funds were hit by leverage and Madoff.
May 2008 in China: closed a $1B+ book, took 80% of chips off the table and bought coal puts — long China commodities/EM, short US banks, after asking 'what if trade financing dries up?'
He reads conviction, not polls: at dinners he tallies the room's billions; when everyone with capital says 'never' on Bitcoin, the odds priced in are close to zero.
Bitcoin is 'the most asymmetric bet I've ever made' — a bet on fiat assets vs something with no fundamentals; Bayesian updating, no preconceived notions.
Traded against LTCM in Brazilian preferred vs ordinary shares in 1998 as the spread kept widening.

quote.text: I have an asymmetric bet in my head that is based not on the next two years, the next three years, but it's based on what I think will be happening to all fiat assets relative to something that has no fundamentals.

themes.watch: Jordi says he has 'a lot of money on that bet' — a large personal Bitcoin position behind his bull case.

themes.title: Ghost rails: crypto was built for humans who don't care — agents will use it
themes.lead: Jordi's bull case is '100% AI agents': software users will chase every spread banks live on, making crypto a margin-compression trade.
bullets: 'Bitcoin's silent IPO' (last year): OG whales selling (e.g. Galaxy's 80,000 BTC sale in July) mirror internet holders in 2000-03 and Google after 2004; government acceptance plus the ETF was the **sell-the-news** event, with altcoins and the SBR hype signalling it.
Ghost rails, after China's ghost cities (his 2006-12 trips, Macau cash flows): rails get built before the users arrive — and the users are agents, since wealthy people don't want faster wires.

Short friction: JPMorgan's net interest income of $107B since 2022 'shouldn't exist'; bank deposits up under 10% vs **money market funds up 70%+**. Stripe and Canton offer yield; Clarity failed, so no stablecoin-yield ban.

Crypto means cryptography: agent swarms and soaring hacking (Meta's Muse, OpenAI solving math problems) make provable ownership — even code IP on-chain — essential. Crypto is $3-4T against $900T of hackable, friction-laden assets.

Banks launching stablecoins = retailers launching websites against Amazon: a sign they feel the threat. Tech went from 13% of the S&P in 2007 to **56%**; VC and private equity have cost money since 2017.

24/7 markets: Korea aims for full tokenization by 2027, Japan too; Druckenmiller buying into Hyperliquid (oil traded there over the Iran weekend). Prime brokers will remark books on weekends — 'the destruction of hedge funds'.
Trust: crypto 'leads with a hoodie', but SVB's run and Bank of America's $1B+ fraud fine (stock -8%) show TradFi is no different.

quote.text: I don't meet wealthy people who go, I wish I could settle a wire in seconds. They don't care.

themes.title: AI isn't a bubble — it's a concentration that rates are making brutal
themes.lead: No valuation, credit or supply bubble exists, but higher yields crush the zombie companies and the debt-dependent parts of the buildout.
bullets: Three bubble types: valuation (dot-com), credit/fraud (housing), oversupply. Nvidia at **15x earnings** vs Cisco's 100x; no fraudulent lending; compute demand still exceeds supply.
Adoption gap: ~5% of office workers use agents vs ~50% in coding and engineering — demand for compute keeps growing as Muse and others spread.
Losers outnumber winners: homebuilders 'get screwed' as AI buildout crowds out borrowers; ZIRP-era zombies that issued 30-50 year debt suffer as rates rise.

First stress: the **Neoclouds**, since data centers are a financing, memory and chip-cost business; Google, Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI 'don't care'. Broadcom and Intel said capital is now the bottleneck.
AI debt is ~5-6% of the buildout; hyperscaler debt is tiny next to equity, and there's an asset side (compute, long-term contracts).
A 20% S&P correction is possible — there were ones in 2018, COVID, 2022 and 2025's tariffs, plus a 10% dip in February — but that isn't a bubble.
Memory stocks 'are going to be very important'; Korea is the overnight AI trade — US AI names gap on KOSPI moves and then barely move.

quote.text: The impact that rates are having is not creating a bubble. It's creating a concentration where there are so many losers and so few winners.

themes.title: When AI kills every moat, Bitcoin's belief is the one left — and wealth becomes money
themes.lead: Jordi rejects 'debasement hedge': Bitcoin wins because competition compresses every company's multiple while belief, like gold's, endures.
bullets: Schumpeter (creative destruction ending in socialism), Milton Friedman and Ray Kurzweil's singularity: AI speeds disruption until no moat survives — hence UBI talk and presidents mailing checks.
Zombie incumbents: **McDonald's** asking franchisees to spend $1M remodelling while out-innovated and hit by Ozempic-style drugs.

Three lasting beliefs: gold (shells and tulips failed), religion, Santa Claus. First fiat — Marco Polo saw China's mulberry-bark money around 1200. Hundreds of millions chose Bitcoin as the store of value.
S&P up ~13% YTD while earnings grew ~33%, Anthropic ARR surprised, capex revised up — multiple compression means nobody trusts moats beyond 3 years. Bitcoin 'doesn't have to deal with that'.
Not a liquidity trade: Bitcoin has tracked, not beaten, the Mag 7 for eight years. Next phase: Mag 7 multiples compress while Bitcoin outperforms — equities are only $150T of the $900T in assets.

'When wealth becomes money': tokenized property (a swap on your house's economics, Miami vs Maine) turns illiquid wealth into M2/M3, reducing the need to print — Lyn Alden's 'nothing stops this train' is the opposing view.
Second fix: tax corporations, since humanoids will be owned by the powerful, first adopters are quant funds and the Mag 7 (UnitedHealth is slow), and individuals move states.

quote.text: Once it goes greed will kick in.

takeaways.title: Use the falling 50-week average (~$77K) as the Bitcoin bull/bear line instead of chasing the exact low.
Consider hedging equities while the S&P sits ~3% off highs into hot CPI and heavy debt issuance.
Gauge consensus by the questions sharp money asks, not their bullish/bearish answers.
Move idle business cash out of zero-yield deposits — the spread is exactly what agents will arbitrage.
Separate AI winners with fortress balance sheets from rate-dependent builders like Neoclouds and ZIRP zombies.
Watch the KOSPI and memory names overnight — they set the US AI open.

hot_takes.take: Crypto is actually about margin compression.
Nvidia is trading at 15 times earnings. So we don't have a valuation bubble.
All old industrial businesses that are still left in the S&P 500 are dead zombie companies for the most part.
It's a bad marketing thing to lead with a hoodie.
Hundreds of millions of people around the globe have chosen Bitcoin as the accepted store of value.
You know my thesis for this year has been you know four year cycle is going to play out.

claims.claim: Bitcoin is near its four-year-cycle bottom and will make fresh all-time highs in the coming years.
The 50-week moving average is the Bitcoin bull/bear line.
Government bailouts and QE arrive within six to 18 months.
Q3 tech earnings, the midterm election and a possible Iran resolution are upcoming positive catalysts.
The equity flows picture for 2027 is as bad as it has been since 2004 as tech issues equity for data centers.
Korea moves to full tokenization of its market, making 24/7 trading of AI-linked stocks the global reference.
Bitcoin outperforms the Mag 7 in the next phase as their multiples compress.
Governments shift to taxing corporations as humanoids replace jobs.
The economy with humanoids will be unrecognizable, with speed and cryptographic safety the key factors.

other_news.title: Sources referenced: Paul Tudor Jones, Lyn Alden, Charlie Munger, Jeff Bezos ('your margin is my opportunity'), Schumpeter, Milton Friedman, Ray Kurzweil, Singularity University, *The Big Short*, What Bitcoin Did with Danny Knowles, and Jordi's Visser Labs papers.

Jordi's 2013 pivot: China's ghost cities and Draghi's 2012 'line in the sand' ended the industrial era for him; he moved his focus to Silicon Valley and exponential tech, while Amazon kept rising with 'no valuation' — like Bitcoin.
